title: node-forge accepts forged RSA signatures with public exponent e=3 and can exhaust ASN.1 parser resources
summary: Non-canonical DigestInfo encodings permit signature forgery for RSA keys with public exponent e=3. Separate nested BIT STRING decoding flaws bypass depth limits and consume excessive CPU or memory.

severity.rationale: Practical signature forgery requires an unusual RSA verification key with public exponent e=3. The parser issue causes denial of service, placing these conditions in the rubric's 30-day category.

affected.note: Both advisories list versions through 1.4.0 inclusive.

exposure: Exposed when verifying attacker-provided signatures with RSA keys with public exponent e=3 or parsing untrusted DER/PEM. Higher-level certificate, PKCS and TLS APIs can reach the affected parser.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.details: Upgrade node-forge to 1.4.1 or later. Avoid RSA verification keys with public exponent e=3. Disabling BIT STRING decoding is only a limited direct-parser workaround and changes parsed structures.
remediation.risk: Medium. Updating and restarting can interrupt dependent workflows.

verification: Confirm the installed version and the component used by running processes meet the documented fix or containment condition.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
Narrowed the RSA signature-forgery condition to public exponent e=3 throughout the record after re-reading the reviewed GitHub advisory.
